messages:
steph_support: Customer reported GitHub OAuth failing during mobile deeplink flow — redirect returns 400 and app never receives code. They say it worked before a proxy change.
raj_eng: any error body from our callback? 400 message?
steph_support: yes. raw callback logs show: \n```
GET /auth/callback?code=SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA&state=eyJzIjoiYWJjLzEyMyJ9 400 - state mismatch
```
steph_support: note the state contains a slash in the encoded payload: original state was base64 of JSON that included "/" char. looks like our proxy or deeplink is normalizing/removing it.
sam_infra: deploy-bot shows cloudfront edge config rollout ~2h ago :deploy-bot: — could be path normalization rule.
raj_eng: repro steps please (browser + mobile). we need the exact redirect uri and how the deeplink is constructed.
steph_support: repro steps from customer: \n1) click GitHub login on mobile webview (in-app browser)\n2) GitHub redirects to https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=<state_b64>\n3) our page does window.location = 'myapp://auth?callback=' + encodeURIComponent(location.href) to hand off to native app\n4) native app opens myapp://auth?callback=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback%3Fcode%3D...%26state%3DeyJzIjoiYWJjLzEyMyJ9
steph_support: but customer shows final deeplink arriving at our proxy as: `myapp://auth?callback=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com%2Fauth%2Fcallback%3Fcode%3D...%26state%3DeyJzIjoiYWJjMTIzIn0` — note the `Lz` (encoded '/') turned into nothing; state truncated and invalid.
raj_eng: hmm that means either our proxy or the OS is un-escaping and then re-encoding the callback querystring, and path separators inside the state are being interpreted as path segments and then stripped.
sam_infra: cloudfront compress/normalize/strip-duplicate-slashes had a fix in the rollout. it might apply to any URL-decoded path segments. rolling back edge rule for signed cookies might help.
jess_security: also check PKCE verifier length match. if state truncated, we could still be receiving correct code but we reject due to missing state->session mapping. is our session stored in cookie? how long is the state? could it be split across cookie chunks?
steph_support: session flow: we store state in a server-side session keyed by a session cookie (sid). The deeplink approach relies on returning the full callback URL back to server via the proxy; if the callback param gets mangled, the server never sees the original state. customer logs show sid cookie intact.
raj_eng: quick mitigation: accept oauth callback that carries code and find a fallback session via a short-lived nonce in a cookie or try URL-decoded variants of state. but don't widen tolerance too much.
raj_eng: can you paste a curl of the exact final request arriving at our frontend? e.g. curl -i 'https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=...&state=...'
steph_support: pasted minimal curl captured by customer below: \n```
GET /auth/callback?code=SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA&state=eyJzIjoiYWJjMTIzIn0 HTTP/1.1\nHost: app.example.com\nUser-Agent: MobileAppWebView/1.2\nCookie: sid=abc123; other=foo
```
raj_eng: that state decodes to {"s":"abc123"} vs expected {"s":"abc/123"} — slash removed. suggests intermediate URL-decoding then path normalization.
sam_infra: action: rolling back CloudFront normalizer for path canonicalization on edge pool a/b to see if it fixes. doing now.
sam_infra: rolled back on pool-a. pls repro, steph.
steph_support: customer confirmed pool-a rollback fixed it for their region :thumbsup:
steph_support: root cause: cloudfront path normalization was un-escaping encoded '/' inside query param callbacks when the callback was re-encoded into a path during deeplink handoff. that produced state truncation.
jess_security: long-term fix options: \n- change deeplink to pass transient session id instead of full callback URL (less fragile)\n- store state server-side and tie to sid cookie; avoid round-trip inside callback param\n- restrict edge normalization to not touch percent-encoded chars in querystring-encoded values (if possible)
raj_eng: priority: implement transient session id + server-side mapping. I'll open an RFC for changes to deeplink flow and PKCE fallbacks.
steph_support: updated ticket and sent customer workaround instructions (use browser login or upgrade to our latest mobile SDK which uses session-id approach). marking as resolved pending eng RFC.
steph_support: closing thread, will re-open if rollout rollback doesn't hold.
